coverage.evidence_note: Corpus documents an Engineering Manager role from Jan 2023 to present, managing six backend engineers. The record does not state a total tenure length, so whether it reaches 3+ years is not established in writing.
Corpus states he hired three engineers onto the team and ran the technical interview loop for each.
The corpus does not mention performance reviews, calibration, or promotion processes anywhere in the management record.
Corpus states he owns the team's quarterly budget for cloud infrastructure spend; a boundary note clarifies this authority does not extend beyond that line.

Corpus documents a progression from Junior Software Engineer (2018) to Software Engineer to Senior Software Engineer leading design of an internal deployment tool, before the 2023 move into management.

Corpus documents running the team's incident postmortem process for platform outages, plus on-call rotation participation and shadowing an on-call engineer during a production incident. Leading live incident response itself is not described.
Corpus states he represents the platform team in quarterly planning with the infrastructure and security orgs.
Corpus documents mentoring two junior engineers during their first year, which is adjacent, but says nothing directly about feedback practice or its quality.

Corpus documents setting the team's roadmap for migrating internal services to Kubernetes, and earlier proposing a tooling change the team adopted. It does not describe how senior engineers were involved in roadmap-setting.

Boundary notes state he has not worked in a regulated industry such as healthcare, and has not built or operated any payment processing system; the Amberlake billing work used a third-party processor with no custom settlement logic.
Corpus states he set the team's roadmap for migrating internal services to the company's new Kubernetes platform.

Corpus documents hiring three engineers onto a team that now numbers six, but a boundary note states he has never managed a team larger than six people, so growth to a larger org is not in the record.
Corpus documents a short internal talk on the team's testing practices; no external or conference speaking is recorded, and a boundary note states he has not published research.
A boundary note states he has not owned a company-wide technical strategy, and that the quarterly planning role at Northfield is representational rather than a strategy-setting mandate.

draft.text:
Engineering Manager, Platform Team — Northfield Cloud (Jan 2023 – Present)
• Lead a team of six backend engineers responsible for the internal deployment platform that other engineering teams depend on to ship.
• Own the team's quarterly budget for cloud infrastructure spend, holding direct accountability for the line rather than contributing estimates to someone else's.
• Hired three engineers onto the team, designing and running the technical interview loop for each.
• Set the team's technical roadmap for migrating internal services onto the company's new Kubernetes platform.
• Run the team's incident postmortem process for platform outages, turning production incidents into documented follow-up work.
• Represent the platform team in quarterly planning with the infrastructure and security orgs, carrying platform concerns into cross-org conversations.

Senior Software Engineer, Platform Team — Northfield Cloud (Jun 2021 – Jan 2023)
• Led the design of the platform team's internal deployment tool, now used across other engineering teams.
• Built and maintained on-call rotation tooling used by three engineering teams; proposed the team's move to a standard on-call rotation tool, which was adopted.
• Mentored two junior engineers through their first year on the team.
• Cut onboarding time for engineers new to the platform by rewriting the setup documentation.

Software Engineer — Amberlake Systems (Aug 2019 – Jun 2021)
• Built internal tooling for provisioning developer environments, including a fix for a recurring race condition in the provisioning queue.
• Worked on the backend services team supporting the company's billing system (third-party payment processor; no custom settlement logic).
• Helped migrate the team's services from a monolith into several smaller services.
• Wrote integration tests for the notification service and participated in the on-call rotation for internal tooling.
• Gave a short internal talk on the team's testing practices.

Junior Software Engineer — Ridgeline Analytics (Jul 2018 – Aug 2019)
• Built data-processing scripts for the analytics team and fixed bugs in the internal reporting tool.
• Set up the team's first shared staging environment; wrote unit tests for a new API endpoint.
• Shadowed the on-call engineer through a production incident.

Profile
• Five years hands-on as a backend and platform engineer (TypeScript and Python) before moving into engineering management in Jan 2023.
• Management scope to date: a single platform team of six engineers — hiring, mentoring, roadmap, budget, and postmortems.
• Not from a regulated-industry or payments background, and has not held a company-wide strategy mandate; strongest fit is deep, hands-on ownership of a platform team.

job.raw_text:
Engineering Manager, Platform Team
Nimbus Cloudworks - Hybrid (Berlin) or Remote (EU)

Who we are

Nimbus Cloudworks makes the internal developer platform that other companies build
their own platforms on top of. Our Platform team is the backbone of the engineering
org: deployment tooling, on-call standards, and the infrastructure everyone else
depends on to ship.

The role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead our Platform team through its next phase
of growth. You'll manage a small group of backend engineers, own the team's roadmap
and budget, and be the person who represents platform concerns when the rest of the
company is planning. We want someone who has been a hands-on engineer before and
still remembers what that's like.

What you'll own

- Directly managing a team of software engineers: hiring, growth, and performance
- The team's budget for cloud infrastructure spend
- Running incident response and postmortems when platform services go down
- Representing the team in quarterly cross-org planning
- Setting the team's technical roadmap in partnership with senior engineers

What we're looking for

- 3+ years directly managing a team of software engineers, including hiring and
  performance reviews
- Experience owning a team budget, not just contributing estimates to one
- A background as a hands-on software engineer before moving into management
- Experience running incident response and postmortems for production outages
- Comfortable representing the team in cross-org planning conversations
- Genuinely good at giving feedback that people can act on

Nice to have

- Experience in a regulated industry such as payments or healthcare
- Familiarity with Kubernetes or a comparable orchestration platform
- Experience scaling a team from a handful of engineers to a larger one
- Public speaking or conference experience
- Experience setting a company-wide technical strategy, not just a team one

What we offer

Competitive compensation, a relocation package if you need one, generous parental
leave, and a team that has been through an incident or two together. Nimbus
Cloudworks is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.
